correctness.rationale: All relevant pair/triple intersection face formulas were checked from block-count inequalities. The triple intersection has H2=Z^(xyz) and H1=direct sum of binom(n_i,2) terms. Every pair intersection has primitive inclusion of the B second-homology lattice and free H1/H2/H3 as computed by integral Mayer–Vietoris. The triple-to-pairs first-homology differential is an isomorphism, while the second-homology map is split-injective. Thus the integral Cech spectral sequence yields precisely ranks B3 and B4, with no extensions or torsion. Since the union is simply connected, H2=0 gives two-connectedness. A 4-dimensional homotopy-colimit CW model and the low Whitehead exact sequence yield a sphere-wedge equivalence. Boundary ranks were exhaustively checked over GF2, GF3 and GF5 for smaller examples and exact integral Smith forms for two finite examples; this last finite evidence is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The question is a natural new three-facet test of the 2026 tolerance-complex bounds, not a manufactured numerical slice. The result is a full three-parameter family of integral homotopy types, including a sharp transition from only three-spheres to two sphere dimensions, a closed multiplicity formula, and an exact infinite family (2,3,m) with growing four-dimensional homology. Generic Leray and collapsibility bounds do not give these ranks or exclude torsion, and an isolated nine-vertex calculation cannot imply the family. The primitive lattice argument is structurally required, not a routine numerical check.
